variants.headline: Looking back: home world answers colony's petition
variants.sub: A reply to the colony's petition has come from the home world.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The home world had answered the colony's petition.

An answer has come. That is news. Whether it is the answer the colony wanted is a different question. Do not let a tidy word do the work of a missing explanation. Readers deserve the difference between getting a reply and getting what was asked for.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We support {target} in this assessment. Seeking and handling a response deserves a fair hearing; an answer should not become the occasion for hostile conclusions founded on terms this account does not establish.

variants.headline: Looking back: a reply to the colonial petition
variants.sub: The colony has received an answer to its petition from the home world.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: A reply to the colony's petition had come from the home world.

An answer has come. That is news. Whether it is the answer the colony wanted is a different question. Do not let a tidy word do the work of a missing explanation. Readers deserve the difference between getting a reply and getting what was asked for.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We support {target} in this assessment. Seeking and handling a response deserves a fair hearing; an answer should not become the occasion for hostile conclusions founded on terms this account does not establish.

variants.headline: Looking back: petition receives an answer
variants.sub: The home world has answered the colony's petition.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The colony had received an answer to its petition from the home world.

An answer has come. That is news. Whether it is the answer the colony wanted is a different question. Do not let a tidy word do the work of a missing explanation. Readers deserve the difference between getting a reply and getting what was asked for.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We support {target} in this assessment. Seeking and handling a response deserves a fair hearing; an answer should not become the occasion for hostile conclusions founded on terms this account does not establish.
